entries.line: Facing a senior or staff interview, leave able to separate graded signal (scope, trade-offs, operability) from a technology tour.
entries.title: What the interviewer is grading

entries.line: Facing a one-line problem, leave able to lock behavior, constraints, and non-goals before any box is drawn.
entries.title: Vague problem to requirements

entries.line: Facing a blank estimate, leave able to compute QPS, storage, and bandwidth out loud with every assumption visible.
entries.title: Capacity math out loud

entries.line: Facing pressure to draw servers, leave able to put endpoints, retention, and the real lookup key down first.
entries.title: API and data model first

entries.line: Facing pressure to distribute immediately, leave able to show a correct single box and the first limit that forces a split.
entries.title: One box, and why it breaks

entries.line: Facing a sketch that will not take questions, leave able to redraw context, whiteboard, read path, and write path from memory.
entries.title: A diagram that survives

entries.line: Facing a closed-book timer, leave able to run the pastebin in about 35 minutes with no notes, score it, and file the first design-log entry.
entries.title: Timed dry run (pastebin)

entries.line: Facing a saturated process, leave able to split a stateless app tier and say where session and file state still sit.
entries.title: The second box

entries.line: Facing uneven load, leave able to choose balancing, health checks, and drain behavior and what each does to in-flight work.
entries.title: Load balancing and draining

entries.line: Facing a database melted by reads, leave able to add cache-aside and name the miss path and what must not be cached.
entries.title: Cache-aside for the melted read

entries.line: Facing a hot pastebin key, leave able to stop a stampede without treating a TTL as invalidation.
entries.title: Hot-key stampede

entries.line: Facing a query the current store cannot serve, leave able to choose SQL or NoSQL from the access pattern and name what you give up.
entries.title: SQL or NoSQL from the broken query

entries.line: Facing a durability or read-scale wall, leave able to add replicas and refuse a lagging replica for reads that cannot lie.
entries.title: Replication and the lagging read

entries.line: Facing large bodies in the database, leave able to move bytes to object storage and name the orphan-object failure.
entries.title: Object storage for the body

entries.line: Facing origin bandwidth on public reads, leave able to place a CDN and say what stays origin-authoritative.
entries.title: CDN in front of public bytes

entries.line: Facing work that should not block the response, leave able to add a queue and describe the backlog the user can see.
entries.title: Queue for work the user does not wait on

entries.line: Facing a public write API, leave able to put rate limits and abuse control on the path before the expensive store.
entries.title: Rate limits and abuse

entries.line: Facing cache or storage nodes that come and go, leave able to use consistent hashing and say when a fixed slot map is simpler.
entries.title: Consistent hashing when nodes change

entries.line: Facing a dependency slower than arrivals, leave able to apply backpressure or shed load and say who feels it.
entries.title: Backpressure and load shedding

entries.line: Facing a slow dependency, leave able to set timeouts and retries so a blip cannot multiply into a storm.
entries.title: Timeouts and retry storms

entries.line: Facing a design that only works at the average, leave able to redo the estimate with fan-out and a stated cache-hit assumption.
entries.title: Capacity redo with visible assumptions

entries.line: Facing tenants on one cluster, leave able to cap a noisy neighbor so one key cannot spend the whole budget.
entries.title: Noisy neighbor and fairness

entries.line: Facing one tangled picture, leave able to narrate the read path and the write path as separate sequences.
entries.title: Read path and write path

entries.line: Facing a large jump in traffic, leave able to name the first component that breaks and the fix you would reach for next.
entries.title: The order-of-magnitude break

entries.line: Facing "what if this dies," leave able to overlay one dependency failure and the user-visible result.
entries.title: Failure overlay on the pastebin

entries.line: Facing a full interview on the spine, leave able to assemble the distributed pastebin in one interview-shaped pass.
entries.title: End-to-end distributed pastebin

entries.line: Facing your own finished design, leave able to find the holes a staff interviewer would open and patch the reasoning.
entries.title: Red-team before they do

entries.line: Facing an interview problem that is not the pastebin, leave able to design image upload and thumbnails from the product behavior, then log a self-score.
entries.title: Mock: image upload and thumbnails

entries.line: Facing the word "consistent," leave able to state the guarantee per operation instead of one label for the whole system.
entries.title: The guarantee per operation

entries.line: Facing a demand for linearizability, leave able to say which operations need it and which you will refuse.
entries.title: Linearizability and what you refuse

entries.line: Facing one hot database, leave able to pick a partition key and say what hash versus range gives up.
entries.title: Partition key, hash, and range

entries.line: Facing a celebrity key, leave able to salt or split it without destroying the lookup you still need.
entries.title: Hot keys and salting

entries.line: Facing stale or thundering cache entries, leave able to choose invalidation or TTL and the stale window you accept.
entries.title: Invalidation and TTL

entries.line: Facing replica lag, leave able to give the right operations monotonic reads or read-your-writes.
entries.title: Lag, monotonic reads, read-your-writes

entries.line: Facing a quorum design, leave able to explain what N, R, and W buy and the unavailable or stale outcome you took.
entries.title: Quorums in plain language

entries.line: Facing a single-writer partition, leave able to treat leader election as a dependency with an unavailable window, not as a protocol lecture.
entries.title: A leader is a dependency

entries.line: Facing retries, leave able to make an at-least-once write safe with idempotency keys and name what can still arrive twice.
entries.title: Idempotency on an at-least-once path

entries.line: Facing a consumer that can see a message twice, leave able to dedupe with an inbox and a defined retention for those keys.
entries.title: Dedupe and the inbox

entries.line: Facing a write that must also become a message, leave able to replace a dual write with an outbox.
entries.title: Outbox, not dual write

entries.line: Facing a multi-row change, leave able to draw the transaction at one shard and pick an isolation level on purpose.
entries.title: Transactions that stop at the shard

entries.line: Facing a workflow that crosses partitions, leave able to use a saga and name the compensation and the crash window.
entries.title: Sagas and compensation

entries.line: Facing two writers, leave able to choose versions, last write, or a merge, and say when a CRDT is worth naming.
entries.title: Conflicts you can explain

entries.line: Facing users in more than one region, leave able to choose a write topology and the conflict or failover cost that comes with it.
entries.title: Active-passive or active-active

entries.line: Facing order across machines, leave able to pick ids and a clock story and name the reorder bug you still have.
entries.title: Clocks, ids, and order

entries.line: Facing a schema that must change, leave able to plan expand, backfill, and cutover without stopping writes, plus a rollback.
entries.title: Schema change and backfill

entries.line: Facing a delete, leave able to use tombstones and retention so replicas and indexes do not resurrect the row.
entries.title: Delete, tombstone, retention

entries.line: Facing an extra index or replica, leave able to state the write amplification, storage class, or egress you just bought.
entries.title: Secondary indexes and data-path cost

entries.line: Facing the end of the data section, leave able to close on guarantee, partition plan, and the failure you accept.
entries.title: Close the data chapter

entries.line: Facing a problem that is not this week's schema, index, or retention lesson, leave able to reserve inventory so two buyers cannot take the last unit, then log a self-score.
entries.title: Mock: warehouse inventory reservation

entries.line: Facing a redirect path, leave able to design create and redirect so a hot link cannot pin one row or one cache key.
entries.title: URL shortener

entries.line: Facing a home feed, leave able to choose fan-out-on-write or fan-out-on-read from follower skew, with ranking models left out.
entries.title: News feed

entries.line: Facing one author with a huge audience, leave able to hybrid-fan-out so a single post cannot stampede storage or the online cluster.
entries.title: Celebrity fan-out

entries.line: Facing two people messaging, leave able to keep per-conversation order, receipts, and offline catch-up without a global total order.
entries.title: One-to-one chat

entries.line: Facing a huge room, leave able to serve history and fan-out without copying every message to every member on the send path.
entries.title: Large-room chat

entries.line: Facing a user who is not in the app, leave able to design push plus an inbox with preferences, dedupe, and a dead provider.
entries.title: Notifications

entries.line: Facing a prefix box, leave able to serve suggestions from a popularity-biased index and bound how stale a suggestion may be.
entries.title: Typeahead

entries.line: Facing catalog search rather than a prefix, leave able to query an inverted index with facets and explain lag after a write.
entries.title: Product search

entries.line: Facing a long video, leave able to take upload through transcode to CDN playback without bytes sitting on the app tier.
entries.title: Video on demand

entries.line: Facing a live stream, leave able to ingest with adaptive bitrate and survive the stampede when the stream starts.
entries.title: Live video

entries.line: Facing "what is near me," leave able to index points, bound staleness, and avoid leaking a precise location.
entries.title: Nearby

entries.line: Facing assigned seats, leave able to hold specific seats with a TTL so you neither oversell nor lock the whole venue.
entries.title: Ticket booking

entries.line: Facing a firehose of measurements, leave able to ingest points with a cardinality limit so one tenant cannot blow the store.
entries.title: Metrics ingestion

entries.line: Facing an unseen problem, leave able to design a job scheduler with leases, missed fires, and duplicate runs, not this week's search, video, location, ticket, or metrics lessons.
entries.title: Mock: job scheduler

entries.line: Facing graphs and pages rather than ingest, leave able to query downsampled series and stop one alert rule from paging on every blip.
entries.title: Metrics query and alerts

entries.line: Facing money movement, leave able to authorize and capture against an idempotent ledger so a retry cannot move money twice.
entries.title: Payments

entries.line: Facing a provider and a ledger that disagree, leave able to find the mismatch and repair it without a silent rewrite of history.
entries.title: Payment reconciliation

entries.line: Facing two editors in one document, leave able to persist concurrent edits and presence and say what you do when they diverge.
entries.title: Collaborative document

entries.line: Facing folders that must match across devices, leave able to sync chunks, resolve conflicts, and survive a client clock that lies.
entries.title: File sync

entries.line: Facing a purchase, leave able to snapshot price and hold stock so a retry cannot double-charge or double-commit inventory.
entries.title: Cart and checkout

entries.line: Facing an arrival spike on scarce stock, leave able to queue buyers with a fairness rule instead of letting them pile onto the database.
entries.title: Flash sale

entries.line: Facing follow and block, leave able to store the graph so a privacy check stays correct on the read path.
entries.title: Social graph

entries.line: Facing posts that must disappear, leave able to fan them out with a TTL that is real in storage and caches, not only in the UI.
entries.title: Ephemeral stories

entries.line: Facing the public web as input, leave able to run a polite frontier with dedupe and freshness so one host is not melted.
entries.title: Web crawler

entries.line: Facing buy and sell orders, leave able to match one instrument on a single sequence and rebuild the book after the matcher crashes.
entries.title: Order book

entries.line: Facing a risky rollout, leave able to serve a flag or kill switch at low latency and bound how stale a client may be.
entries.title: Feature flags

entries.line: Facing "who did that," leave able to append a queryable activity log with retention and a tamper claim you can actually keep.
entries.title: Audit log

entries.line: Facing an unseen product, leave able to design a large email inbox (ingest, folders, search, attachments), not this week's graph, stories, crawler, book, flags, or audit lessons.
entries.title: Mock: email inbox

entries.line: Facing a vague reliability ask, leave able to state an SLO and the user-visible miss when it is breached.
entries.title: SLOs and the miss a user sees

entries.line: Facing a sick dependency rather than a total outage, leave able to pick a degraded mode and what you refuse to drop.
entries.title: Degradation under partial failure

entries.line: Facing a region that is already dark, leave able to state RPO, RTO, and which side is authoritative for new writes.
entries.title: Losing a region

entries.line: Facing an on-call question, leave able to name the dashboard, the page, and the first runbook step for a failure you designed.
entries.title: Observability that pages a human

entries.line: Facing a design that is correct and expensive, leave able to cut replicas, egress, or retention and say the user-visible risk.
entries.title: Cost as a spoken trade-off

entries.line: Facing a system that must change shape, leave able to migrate with a dual path and a rollback while writes continue.
entries.title: Migration while live

entries.line: Facing a dispatch problem that is not an SLO or migration lecture, leave able to design matching and, near minute 25, lose a region or the location store.
entries.title: Mock: delivery dispatch with a late failure

entries.line: Facing the last mocks without a shared ritual, leave able to run a timer, the senior rubric, and a design log, and see where the separate kit plugs in.
entries.title: Kit hookup and the design log

entries.line: Facing a read-heavy problem that is not the kit-setup lesson, leave able to design article serving with hot pages and invalidation on publish, inside the time box.
entries.title: Mock: article serving (read-heavy)

entries.line: Facing the day-86 writeup, leave able to score it on the senior rubric and rewrite only the weakest section into the design log.
entries.title: Debrief: read-heavy mock

entries.line: Facing a write-heavy problem, leave able to design event intake with dedupe, late events, and a durable sink, and leave a complete design-log entry.
entries.title: Mock: event intake (write-heavy)

entries.line: Facing the day-88 writeup, leave able to score it, compare it with day 86, and log the one staff-level gap to close before the final mock.
entries.title: Debrief: write-heavy mock

entries.line: Facing a realtime interview with no lesson beside it, leave able to run the kit's current problem (fallback: multiplayer lobby) and leave the design log as the only artifact.
entries.title: Mock: realtime lobby (kit run)

phases.label: Hearing the problem
phases.question: Install the hour: requirements and numbers before boxes, then a diagram you can redraw. Pastebin is the worked example.

phases.label: First distributed design
phases.question: Each new box is a fix for a break in the pastebin, not a catalog of tools. Day 28 is a different problem. Do not treat this map as the boxes that mock requires.

phases.label: Data and consistency
phases.question: Guarantees, keys, and the failure you accept. The pastebin is still the worked example. Consensus stays a dependency; Raft is appendix reading, not this phase. Day 49 is a different problem. Do not treat this map as the design that mock requires.

phases.label: Product-shaped systems
phases.question: One product a day, or a variant whose failure mode is new. Inventory on day 49, assigned seats on day 61, and a flash-sale queue on day 70 are three different problems. Ranking models stay out.

phases.label: Failure and senior signal
phases.question: Staff credit is the failure you can operate, pay for, and migrate. Day 84 is a product mock with a scripted outage, not a repeat of these lectures.

phases.label: Mocks and the kit
phases.question: Three full interviews: read-heavy, write-heavy, realtime. Debriefs are their own days. Day 90 is kit-run: no lesson beside the timer. The kit is optional; use the lobby fallback if you do not own it.

tagline: Attempt the problem, then read. Requirements before boxes. One sitting is a day.
title: FAANG System Design, 90 days
